(Code 1981, § 11-39; Ord. No. 1987-3, 11-16-1987)
694:
It shall be unlawful for the owner of a domestic animal or domestic fowl which has died within the city limits of the city to refuse or fail to bury such carcass deep enough to prevent stench therefrom, within three hours after the death of animal or fowl; provided any qualified plant or processor shall be allowed to process or dispose of such carcass in accordance with law. The keeping or maintaining of any carcass beyond three hours after death without burying such carcass or providing for disposal by a qualified plant or processor will be deemed an unhealthful and hazardous condition and is declared a nuisance and is subject to abatement as provided in article IV of this chapter.
(Code 1981, § 11-40; Ord. No. 1987-3, 11-16-1987)
696:
Footnote 4:
State Law reference— Nuisance abatement and lien procedures described under O.C.G.A. § 41-2-9 do not impair or limit in the power of the municipality to define and declare nuisances and cause their removal or abatement by summary proceedings or otherwise, O.C.G.A. § 41-2-9(f).
697: The city council may appoint, or designate that the city manager appoint a city official to exercise the powers prescribed by this article.
698:
(a) Prior to an action for abatement, whenever the existence of any nuisance defined in this chapter, except those sections dealing with animal carcasses or emergency situations, on any lots or parcels of real estate, buildings or structures situated within this city, shall come to the knowledge of a code enforcement officer or chief of police, it shall be the code enforcement officer's duty to make an investigation or inspection of the specific dwelling, building, structure or property. If the officer's investigation or inspection identifies the existence of any nuisance defined in this chapter, except those sections dealing with animal carcasses or emergency situations, upon that specific dwelling, building, structure or property, then the city official may issue a complaint in rem against the lot, tract or parcel of real property on which such dwelling, building, or structure is situated or where such public health hazard or general nuisance exists and shall cause summons and a copy of the complaint to be served on the interested parties for such dwelling, building or structure. The summons shall notify the interested parties that a hearing will be held before the municipal court, at a date and time not less than 15 days nor more than 45 days after the filing of said complaint.
(b) The notice requirement and time period for correction do not apply when dealing with animal carcasses or other emergency situations where the public health, welfare or property are placed in immediate danger by an existing or potentially hazardous, toxic, disease producing or fire producing substance or dilemma. In such situations the city, by and through its elected officials and employees, shall act to protect the citizenry of large from harm.
(Code 1981, § 11-41; Ord. No. 1987-3, 11-16-1987)
699:
(a) If, after such notice and hearing, the court determines that a nuisance condition, as provided in articles I through IV of this chapter, exists on the dwelling, building, structure, or property, then the court shall state in writing findings of fact in support of such determination and shall issue and cause to be served upon the interested parties that have answered the complaint or appeared at the hearing an order:
(1) If the repair, alteration or improvement of the said dwelling, building or structure can be made at a reasonable cost in relation to the present value of the dwelling, building, or structure, requiring the owner, within the time specified in the order, to repair, alter or improve such dwelling, building or structure, so as to bring it into full compliance with the applicable codes relevant to the cited violation and, if applicable, to secure the structure so that it cannot be used in connection with the commission of drug crimes; or
(2) If the repair, alteration, or improvement of the said dwelling, building or structure in order to bring it into full compliance with applicable codes relevant to the cited violations cannot be made at a reasonable cost in relation to the present value of the dwelling, building or structure, requiring the owner, within the time specified in the order, to demolish and remove such dwelling, building or structure, and all debris from the property.
(b) If the owner fails to comply with the court's order to repair or demolish the dwelling, building, or structure, the city official may cause such dwelling, building, or structure to be repaired, altered, or improved or to be vacated and closed or demolished. Such abatement action shall commence within 270 days after the expiration of time specified in the order for abatement by the owner. The city official shall cause to be posted on the main entrance of the building, dwelling, or structure a placard with the following words:
"This building is unfit for human habitation or commercial, industrial or business use and does not comply with the applicable codes or has been ordered secured to prevent its use in connection with drug crimes or constitutes an endangerment to public health or safety as a result of unsanitary or unsafe conditions. The use or occupation of this building is prohibited and unlawful."
(c) If the city official has the structure demolished, reasonable effort shall be made to salvage reusable materials for credit against the cost of demolition. The proceeds of any moneys received from the sale of salvaged materials shall be used or applied against the cost of the demolition and removal of the structure, and proper records shall be kept showing application of sales proceeds. Any such sale of salvaged materials may be made without the necessity of public advertisement and bid. The city official and governing authority are relieved of any and all liability resulting from or occasioned by the sale of any such salvaged materials, including, without limitation, defects in such salvaged materials.
(Code 1981, § 11-42; Ord. No. 1987-3, 11-16-1987)
700:
(a) The amount of the cost of demolition, including all court costs, appraisal fees, administrative costs incurred by the county tax commissioner or municipal tax collector or city revenue officer, and all other costs necessarily associated with the abatement action, including restoration to grade of the real property after demolition, shall be a lien against the real property upon which such cost was incurred.
(b) Lien to attach to real property; procedure for collection.
(1) The lien shall attach to the real property upon the filing of a certified copy of the order requiring repair, closure or demolition in the office of the clerk of superior court in the county where the real property is located and shall relate back to the date of the filing of the lis pendens notice required under O.C.G.A. § 41-2-12(c). The clerk of superior court shall record and index such certified copy of the order in the deed records of the county and enter the lien on the general execution docket. The lien shall be superior to all other liens on the property, except liens for taxes, to which the lien shall be inferior, and shall continue in force until paid.
(2) Upon final determination of costs, fees and expenses incurred in accordance with this chapter, the city official responsible for enforcement actions in accordance with this chapter shall transmit to the appropriate county tax commissioner or municipal tax collector or city revenue officer a statement of the total amount due and secured by said lien, together with copies of all notices provided to interested parties. The statement of the city official shall be transmitted within 90 days of completion of the repairs, demolition, or closure. It shall be the duty of the appropriate county tax commissioner or municipal tax collector or city revenue officer, who is responsible or whose duties include the collection of municipal taxes, to collect the amount of the lien using all methods available for collecting real property ad valorem taxes; provided, however, that the limitation of O.C.G.A. § 48-4-78 which requires 12 months of delinquency before commencing a tax foreclosure shall not apply. A county tax commissioner shall collect and enforce municipal liens imposed pursuant to this chapter in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 48-5-359.1. The county tax commissioner or municipal tax collector or city revenue officer shall remit the amount collected to the governing authority of the county or municipality whose lien is being collected.
(Code 1981, § 11-43; Ord. No. 1987-3, 11-16-1987)
701:
(a) Enforcement of liens pursuant to this section may be initiated at any time following receipt by the county tax commissioner or municipal tax collector or city revenue officer of the final determination of costs in accordance with this chapter. The unpaid lien amount shall bear interest and penalties from and after the date of final determination of costs in the same amount as applicable to interest and penalties on unpaid real property ad valorem taxes. An enforcement proceeding pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-4-78 for delinquent ad valorem taxes may include all amounts due under this chapter.
(b) The redemption amount in any enforcement proceeding pursuant to this article shall be the full amount of the costs as finally determined in accordance with this article together with interest, penalties, and costs incurred by the city council, county tax commissioner, municipal tax collector, or city revenue officer in the enforcement of such lien. Redemption of property from the lien may be made in accordance with the provisions of O.C.G.A. §§ 48-4-80 and 48-4-81.
(c) The city council may waive and release any such lien imposed on property upon the owner of such property entering into a contract with the city agreeing to a timetable for rehabilitation of the real property or the dwelling, building or structure on the property and demonstrating the financial means to accomplish such rehabilitation.
(Code 1981, § 11-44; Ord. No. 1987-3, 11-16-1987)
702:
Enforcement of this chapter may be accomplished by the city in any manner authorized by law or combination thereof, and in addition, any person who by reason of another's violation of any provision of this chapter, who suffers special damage to himself/herself, his/her property or livelihood may bring an action for abatement as allowed in O.C.G.A. § 41-2-1 et seq.
(Code 1981, § 11-45; Ord. No. 1987-3, 11-16-1987)
703:
Violations of this chapter, or any provision herein shall be punished in accordance with the penalties allowed under state law and the general penalties described in section 1-8. Conviction of ordinance violations shall be admissible in the trial or hearing of any abatement proceeding involving the same material facts, O.C.G.A. § 16-7-48.
(Code 1981, § 11-46; Ord. No. 1987-3, 11-16-1987)
704:
(a) The notice and time period for correction required in section 50-126 prior to an abatement proceeding do not apply to the issuance of citations or criminal prosecution. Citations for criminal violations under this chapter may be issued without prior notice. Prior warnings, if any, shall be admissible in the prosecution of any criminal violation under this chapter.
(b) In addition to the procedures and remedies in this article, the city official may issue citations for violations of state minimum standard codes, optional building, fire, life safety and other technical codes adopted by this Code, and conditions creating a public health hazard or general nuisance, and seek to enforce such citations in a court of competent jurisdiction prior to issuing a complaint in rem as provided in this article.
(Code 1981, § 11-47; Ord. No. 1987-3, 11-16-1987)
705:
Footnote 1:
State Law reference— Limitation on expanding the power of municipal regulation over any business activity regulated by the public service commission, O.C.G.A. § 36-35-6(a)(5); business and occupation taxes, O.C.G.A. § 48-13-5 et seq.
707:
The specific and occupation taxes set forth in this chapter are hereby levied and shall be collected in the amount hereinafter specified upon each and every person engaged in the business, trade or profession, or doing acts named or described herein within the corporate limits of the city during each year.
(Code 1981, § 14-1; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 1)
708:
No person shall be engaged in, prosecute or carry on any business, trade or profession, either in whole or in part within the corporate limits of the city by maintaining an office, or engage in any business in any manner without having registered the name of said business with the city clerk and paid occupational tax as hereafter provided.
(Code 1981, § 14-2; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 2)
709:
Each such occupational tax shall be for each calendar year. Said occupational tax shall be due and payable January 1 of each calendar year and shall be delinquent if not paid by March 31 of each calendar year.
(Code 1981, § 14-3; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 3; Ord. No. 2024-08, § (A), 9-10-2024)
711:
All taxes levied on the basis of gross receipts under section 54-12 are levied on accounts of business to be transacted during each calendar year. However, for convenience of both the city and the taxpayer, and to eliminate the necessity of making numerous returns, those businesses subject to the tax levied under section 54-12 shall, on or before the times hereinafter set forth, file with the business license clerk the return or application hereinafter specifically provided for showing the gross receipts of that business during the calendar year immediately preceding the year for which the tax is due. This return or application shall be used as an estimate for making payment of the gross receipts tax for the year which it is filed, the actual and final amount of tax levied for business transacted in said year to be paid in accordance with a final return to be made after the termination of said year in accordance with the procedure hereinafter set forth.
(Code 1981, § 14-5; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 5)
712:
Every person subject to the occupational tax under section 54-12 for each calendar year shall at the end of the preceding year for which tax was due, and on or before March 15 of said year, make a return in writing to the city clerk, on a form supplied by said clerk for the purpose, setting forth under oath the following information:
(1) Style name of the person, firm, company or corporation.
(2) Location at which the trade, business or profession is to be conducted.
(3) Exact nature of the trade, business or profession for which license is requested.
(4) The correct brackets are set forth in the gross brackets classification schedules, that were provided as exhibit B, in the ordinance from which this provision was derived, that includes the full and true amount of the gross sales, receipts, premiums, commissions or other form of measurable returns from the trade, business, or profession during the preceding calendar year. As herein required, the report of gross sales, receipts, premiums, etc., shall include all business done within the state. All the information herein required shall be given under oath by the owner, or a member of the firm, or an officer of a corporation or by an authorized employee having exact knowledge of actual business done.
(5) Where business is solicited, sales are made and goods delivered or transactions are completed and occupational tax paid on same in an incorporated town or city other than the city, this amount shall be deducted from the total receipts and such information shall be furnished with the application.
(Code 1981, § 14-6; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 6; Ord. No. 1995-2, § 2, 3-6-1995)
713:
Where a business subject to the gross receipts tax for a particular calendar year has been conducted for only a part of said year, amount of gross receipts for such a part shall be set forth in said return. The return shall also show a figure putting the receipts for such a part of a year on an annual basis, which figure shall bear a reasonable ratio to the amount of gross receipts for such year as the full year bears to such part. The figure shall be used as the estimate of the gross receipts of the business for the next calendar year.
(Code 1981, § 14-7; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 7)
714:
The amount of tax levied under section 54-12 based on the estimates as set forth in section 54-7, shall be payable to said city at the offices of the city clerk, on January 1 of each year, and delinquent if not paid on or before March 15 of each year.
(Code 1981, § 14-8; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 8)
715:
After the end of each year, and on or before March 15 of each year, the owner, proprietor, manager or executive officer of the business liable for said gross receipts tax levied for the preceding year shall file with the business license clerk of said city a signed and sworn return setting forth the actual amount of correct bracket, are set forth in the gross brackets classification schedules, that were provided as exhibit B, in the ordinance from which this provision was derived, of the gross receipts of said business during the preceding calendar year.
(1) If the amount of the gross receipts tax for the preceding year, based on the return provided for in this section and on the rate of said tax provided for in this chapter exceeds the amount of gross receipts tax theretofore paid by said business based on the estimate filed pursuant to section 54-5, the difference in said amount shall be due and payable by the taxpayer to the city on or before March 15 of the year in which the return is filed, and shall be delinquent if not paid on or before said date.
(2) If the amount of the gross tax for the preceding year, based on the return provided for in this section and on the rate of tax provided for in this chapter, is less than the amount of the gross receipts tax theretofore paid by such business based on the estimate filed pursuant to section 54-5, the difference in said amount shall be refunded by the city to the taxpayer provided application is made therefor by the business within 30 days of its discontinuance; or, if said business continues to be conducted in said city during the year in which said return is filed, such difference in amounts may be credited by the city on the amount of business license tax to be paid to the city by said business for the year in which said return is filed.
(Code 1981, § 14-9; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 9)
716:
If a business is begun for the first time on or before January 1 of any calendar year that this chapter is in effect, then the license fee herein assessed against such business shall be determined as follows: The city clerk, upon registration and application for license for such business shall issue a business license for the year in which said registration and application is made, and the estimated fee for such license shall be computed according to the estimate by the business of its taxable gross revenue for one calendar year. The annual estimated fee, as so determined, shall be divided by 12, in order to arrive at a monthly fee amount. Such monthly fee shall then be multiplied by the actual number of months remaining in said first year of which the business can operate; the product being the estimated license fee for the first year's business operation. The transaction of business during any month, or portion thereof, for the purpose of this provision, shall be deemed to have been the transaction of business for the entire month.
(Code 1981, § 14-10; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 10)
717:
Should any person, firm or corporation be in a business or commence a business not listed in this chapter, then the city clerk of said city shall set the special or license tax on such business. Any person, firm or corporation being dissatisfied with the decision of the said city clerk shall have the right of appeal to the city council, provided said person, firm or corporation makes such appeal in writing to said city council within 30 days of the disputed decision of said city clerk.
(Code 1981, § 14-11; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 11)
718:
(a) For the purpose of this chapter, every person, firm, company or corporation engaged in trade, business, or profession requiring licenses are classified in accordance to their main line of business as defined in the Standard Industrial Classification Manual, Executive Office of the President, Office of Management and Budget, and profitability classes are assigned in accordance with Statistics of Income, Business Income Tax Returns, U.S. Treasury Department, Internal Revenue Service. In the case where a person, firm, company or corporation is engaged in more than one line of business, taxes will be levied on the basis of the dominant business activity of the licensee.
(b) The six separate classifications of class 1 through class 6, that were provided as exhibit A in the ordinance from which this provision was derived, so as to provide for the determination of the occupational tax to be levied as a fixed sum and measured by taxable gross revenue, the purpose of which is to recognize the ability of businesses to pay as determined by nationwide averages. All separate businesses, engaged in more than one business activity, shall be classified on the basis of their dominant business activity, except that persons whose dominant business activity is legally exempted or otherwise limited by city ordinances or by state law from the tax, shall be classified according to his/her principal subsidiary business, if any, which is subject to the levy and assessment of an occupational tax. The subclassification of all businesses within each classification as to fixed units of taxation, that is, bracket ranges of taxable gross revenue against which there are applied fixed rates, are set forth in the gross brackets classification schedules, that were provided as exhibit B, in the ordinance from which this provision was derived.
(c) Determination of license fee herein levied and assessed shall be determined in accordance with the following formula:
(1) Determination of the taxable gross revenue as defined by this chapter and the rules and regulations promulgated in connection therewith.
(2) Classification of the subject business by referring to exhibit A, the classification schedule in the ordinance from which this provision was derived.
(3) Determination of the license fee on volume of gross revenue that was provided as exhibit B, in the ordinance from which this provision was derived, gross brackets classification schedule, using the information as a result of the determination in subsections (c)(1) and (2) of this section.
(Code 1981, § 14-12; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 12)
720:
All licenses under this chapter which are not paid for by March 31 of each calendar year or at the time of commencement of business if after March 31, will bear penalty at the rate of ten percent of the amount due and unpaid [or] $25.00, whichever is greater.
(Code 1981, § 14-14; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 14; Ord. No. 1990-2, 3-19-1990; Ord. No. 2024-08, § (B), 9-10-2024)
721:
Any person or other entity exercising or carrying on any trade, business, profession or operating any establishment within the city, for which a license or payment of an occupation tax is required by this chapter, without first having registered as provided in section 54-2 and paying the appropriate license or occupation fee, shall be liable for a fine not exceeding $200.00. For the purpose of this section, each day for which said license or occupation fee is not paid shall be deemed a new violation and subject to the same penalty.
(Code 1981, § 14-15; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 15; Ord. No. 1989-3, § 1, 4-17-1989)
722:
Occupational license granted under this chapter shall not authorize the holder to exercise or carry on the trade, business, or profession named herein at any other place than that mentioned in said license.
(Code 1981, § 14-16; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 16)
723:
All persons shall exhibit and display the license or occupational tax receipt issued to them in a conspicuous place in their business establishment if any in the city. Any transient or nonresident person, firm or corporation doing business within the city shall carry such license or occupational tax receipt either upon his/her person or in any vehicle or other conveyance which is used in such business and such person shall exhibit the same to any authorized enforcement officer of the city when so requested.
(Code 1981, § 14-17; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 17)
724:
Any person moving from one location to another shall notify the city clerk of such move and the new address in writing on a form provided by the city clerk no later than the day of moving. The same license or receipt for occupational tax will be valid at the new location if said new location conforms to the zoning regulations of the city, as set forth in exhibit A to this Code.
(Code 1981, § 14-18; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 18)
725:
Business licenses or occupational tax receipts shall not be transferable and a transfer of ownership shall be considered in the same light as the termination of such business and the establishment of a new business. Therefore, a new occupational license tax shall be required for the new owner of the business.
(Code 1981, § 14-19; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 19)
726:
Where a business is conducted at more than one location or place, each location or place shall be considered a separate business under the terms of this chapter and a separate occupational license tax shall be levied and paid.
(Code 1981, § 14-20; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 20)
727:
Such license, referred to in this chapter, shall automatically expire on December 31 of the year of its issuance.
(Code 1981, § 14-21; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 21)
728:
Nothing herein contained shall be interpreted so as to require any person who may engage in casual or isolated activity and commercial transactions, where such involve personal assets and are not the principal occupation of the individual, to obtain a business license or pay occupational tax therefor.
(Code 1981, § 14-22; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 22)
729:
Whenever in this chapter, the term "dealer" or "person" is used, as principal, but in his, her or their absence any agent, clerk, or employee shall be subject to the penalties herein imposed, should the said business be carried on without registering and paying the required occupational license tax in the same manner as if he, she or they were the proprietors of said business.
(Code 1981, § 14-23; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 23)
730:
In addition to any other penalties provided hereinbefore for violation of this chapter, in the event any person shall fail to pay the tax provided herein as and when the same has become due, the clerk of the city shall issue an execution against the said person, firm, or corporation so delinquent, and his/her or its property, for the amount of license tax prescribed by this chapter for the carrying-on of said business.
(Code 1981, § 14-24; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 24)
731:
Persons who can qualify for a state veteran's free license must secure such license from the state and present same to the city clerk, who will honor the same and issue a city license.
(Code 1981, § 14-25; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 25)
733:
The city clerk shall administer and enforce the provisions of this chapter for levy, assessment and collection of license fees and penalties imposed herein.
(Code 1981, § 14-27; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 27)
734:
The city clerk shall have the power and authority to make and publish reasonable rules and regulations not inconsistent with this chapter or other laws of the city and the state, or the constitution of the state or the United States, for the administration and enforcement of the provisions of this chapter and the collection of the license or occupational tax hereunder.
(Code 1981, § 14-28; Ord. of 12-15-1980, § 28)
735:
(a) An annual regulatory fee shall be imposed on persons engaged in the following businesses: Every person subject to payment or regulatory fee levied by this chapter shall display a current regulatory fee certificate in a conspicuous place at the location for which such certificate was issued. If a tax payer does not have a permanent location within the city, the regulatory fee certificate shall be shown to any police officer (or any other person charged with enforcing this chapter) upon request.
(b) The amount of the regulatory fee shall be as established by the city council from time to time.
(Code 1981, § 14-29; Ord. No. 1995-2, § 5, 3-6-1995)
738:
(a) It shall be unlawful to operate or conduct a public dance in the city without having first obtained a permit therefor as is herein required.
(b) For the purposes hereof, a public dance is defined as a gathering of people at a public place for the purpose of dancing, irrespective of whether admission is charged or irrespective of whether said dance is open to the general public or by invitation only.
(Code 1981, § 14-30; Ord. of 1-6-1975, § 1)
739:
(a) Application for a permit for a public dance shall be made to the chief of police or the chief's delegate and shall contain the following information:
(1) The full true name and any other names used by the applicant, as well as the name of the person or organization/business entity sponsoring the public dance.
a. If the application is made on behalf of a corporation, partnership, limited liability company, other business entity or civic organization, the name of the corporation, partnership, limited liability company, other business entity or civic organization shall be set forth exactly as shown in its articles of incorporation or charter, together with the place and date of incorporation, place and date of registration, and the names and addresses of each of its current officers and directors. The corporation, partnership, limited liability company, other business entity or civic organization applying for a permit shall attach to the application a copy of its articles of incorporation or bylaws. The corporation, partnership, limited liability company, other business entity or civic organization applying for a permit shall designate one of its officers to act as its responsible managing officer. Such designated person shall complete and sign all application forms required of an individual applicant under this section, but only one application fee shall be charged.
b. If the person, corporation, partnership, limited liability company, other business entity or civic organization on whose behalf the permit is being filed is doing business under a trade name, the applicant shall attach a copy of the registration statement, verified by affidavit, filed with the city clerk.
(2) The present address and telephone number of the applicant and person or organization/business entity sponsoring the public dance.
(3) Date of birth and social security number for the applicant and/or designated managing officer of the organization/business entity sponsoring the public dance.
(4) Acceptable written proof that the applicant and/or designated managing officer of the organization/business entity sponsoring the public dance is at least 18 years of age.
(5) Address of the premises where the public dance will be held, conducted or carried on.
(6) The name and address of the owner and/or lessor of the real property upon which the public dance is to be held, conducted or carried on and a copy of the lease or rental agreement.
(7) The true names and addresses of two responsible persons over the age of 21 who, on the date of the public dance for which a permit is requested, will remain on the premises of the location where the public dance will be held, conducted, or carried on, from the commencement of the public dance until its end thereafter.
(b) Application must be made 30 days prior to the date of the proposed dance and shall be made on forms prepared by the city for that purpose.
(Code 1981, § 14-31; Ord. of 1-6-1975, § 2)
741:
(a) If, as a result of the investigation authorized by this article, the applicant's qualifications or business responsibility are found to be unsatisfactory, the police chief shall write on the application the reasons for such disapproval. Within 14 business days after the date upon which the application was filed, the police chief shall mail to the applicant a notice of denial stating the reasons for denial of the permit. The notice shall be deemed complete when mailed.
(b) The chief of police, in denying an application for a permit, shall be empowered to authorize the conduct of the public dance on a date, at a time, or in a location, different from that named by the applicant. An applicant desiring to accept an alternate permit shall, within five days after notice of the action of the chief of police, file a written notice of acceptance with the chief of police. An alternate permit shall conform to the requirements of and shall have the effect of a permit issued under this article.
(c) No application for a permit will be considered for any applicant who has submitted a prior application which has been denied, withdrawn or otherwise disposed of within the past 30 days.
742:
Upon approval of the chief of police, the city clerk or chief of police shall be authorized to issue a permit for said dance to the person or persons requesting same. There shall be no charge for the issuance of said permit; however, no such permit shall be issued to a person who is not a person of good moral character, nor to a corporation or organization which is not represented by a person of good moral character.
(Code 1981, § 14-33; Ord. of 1-6-1975, § 4)
743: The city manager or the chief of police shall have the authority to revoke or suspend a permit issued under this article upon application of the standards for issuance as set forth in this article.
744:
(a) Any person aggrieved by an adverse permit decision of the chief of police may appeal to the city manager. Notification of appeal to the city manager must be in writing and must be submitted to the city clerk within ten days after notice of the denial was sent to the applicant. The city manager shall act upon the appeal within 14 days after the notification of appeal has been received.
(b) Any person aggrieved by an adverse appeal decision of the city manager may appeal to the city council. Notification of appeal to the city council must be in writing and must be submitted to the city clerk within ten days after the adverse appeal decision of the city manager. The city council shall act upon the appeal within 30 days after the notification of appeal has been received.
745:
It shall be unlawful to conduct a public dance in any hall or place which is not equipped with sufficient and adequate exits of three feet or more in width; no hall or building which is not provided with at least two exits of three feet or more in width shall be used for such purposes.
(Code 1981, § 14-34; Ord. of 1-6-1975, § 5)
746:
Each such public dance shall be attended by at least two police officers, auxiliary or regular, whose duty it shall be to supervise and patrol at said dance. The person or organization sponsoring said dance shall be responsible for all expenses incurred in the hiring of said police officers.
(Code 1981, § 14-35; Ord. of 1-6-1975, § 6)
749:
(a) Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-6-93, there is hereby levied for each calendar year, an annual business license tax upon state and national banking associations, federal savings and loan associations and state building and loan associations a business license tax at the rate of 0.25 percent of the gross receipts of said institutions. The term "gross receipts" means gross receipts as that term is defined in O.C.G.A. § 48-6-93. Notwithstanding any other provisions of this section, the minimum amount of business license tax due from any depository financial institution pursuant to this section shall be $1,000.00 per year.

The following words and phrases shall have the meanings set forth in this section unless the use of any such word or phrase in context clearly indicates otherwise:
Booth, stand means any table, shelf, counter, cart or other facility, whether mobile or fixed, which is placed on a street or other public place within the city for the purpose of selling or offering to sell any goods or service to the public, or for soliciting for any purpose.
City means the mayor and councilmembers of the city, a municipal corporation, and the jurisdictional authority of that municipal corporation.
License means the right or privilege granted by the city to engage in business as a transient merchant or peddler within the corporate limits of the city. Evidence that such right or privilege has been granted shall be in the form of a license document issued by the city treasurer, which document shall be kept at the merchant's place of business within the city or on the peddler's person or within the peddler's vehicle.
Peddler means a person who is selling new or pre-packaged products within the city limits of the City of Alma at a location other than a permanent building or structure licensed by the city.
Permit means the authorization granted by the city to solicit for charitable or religious purposes, or to solicit subscriptions as defined by this chapter there being no fee nor charge for such permit. Evidence that such authorization has been granted shall be in the form of a permit document issued by the city treasurer.
Solicitor for charitable or religious purposes means any person who solicits contributions from the public, either on the streets of the city or from door to door, for any charitable or religious organization, and who does not sell or offer to sell any single item with a cost to the purchaser in excess of $10.00, shall be defined as a "solicitor for charitable or religious purposes." No qualification as a charitable or religious organization shall exist unless the applicant:
(1) Is able to demonstrate a current exemption certificate from the Internal Revenue Service pursuant to section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954; or
(2) Has maintained in the county a continuous existence as a charitable or religious organization for a period of three years prior to the date of its application pursuant to this chapter.
Solicitor for subscriptions means any person who solicits subscriptions by going from place to place within the city, and who offers for sale subscriptions to magazines or other materials protected by the provisions of the First Amendment to the Constitution of the United States of America, shall be defined as a "solicitor for subscriptions."
Street means and includes any street, alley, lane, avenue, court, sidewalk, public right-of-way, or any other public place within the city.
Transient merchant means any person, firm, or corporation, whether resident or nonresident of the city, who has no permanent, regular place of business within the city and who engages in the business of selling or offering to sell goods or services from a temporary fixed place of business located within the city, such temporary places of business to include any room or space in a hotel or motel, boardinghouse, public or private building, or any other fixed place of business within the city; however, no merchant shall be considered a transient merchant under this article if such merchant:
(1) Is a bona fide commercial traveler selling goods at wholesale by samples;
(2) Has already paid a license to the city for the privilege of conducting permanent business;
(3) Is a peddler otherwise licensed by the city to sell goods from place to place; or
(4) Is a civic club, service club or school who, from time to time, engages in the selling of merchandise to the public as a club or school project.
Transient peddler means any person who is a nonresident of the city, who has no permanent, regular place of business within the city, and who engages in the business of selling or offering to sell goods or services by going from place to place within the city, except a person selling agricultural products and holding a letter from a county agent certifying that the products were produced by that person.

(2) No peddler, solicitor or transient merchant shall stand or sit in or near the entrance to any house or place of business, and no peddler or solicitor shall stand or sit in any place which may disrupt or impede pedestrian or vehicular traffic.
(3) No peddler, solicitor or transient merchant shall offer to sell goods or services or solicit in vehicular traffic lanes of the city, and no such peddler or solicitor shall operate a road block directed towards vehicular traffic.
(4) If any officer of the city police department or the revenue department should determine that pedestrian or vehicular traffic congestion is such that a public hazard or inconvenience would result from peddling, soliciting or selling in a congested area, such officer shall have authority to require any peddler or solicitor to move from the area.

Upon request by the building official, the designee of the building official, or any law enforcement officer, the transient merchant, and transient, local peddler or solicitor shall present said written permission from the landowner. In addition to all other requirements of this chapter, and of applicable law the transient merchant, transient peddler, local peddler or solicitor shall notify the police department of the city of the location of the stand or booth wherein such business is to be conducted.

(9) When any officer of the city police department or any other authorized city officer, deems that a peddler, solicitor or transient merchant is in violation of any provision of this chapter, such officer shall have authority to direct the peddler, solicitor or transient merchant to correct the violation immediately, and such peddler, solicitor or transient merchant shall comply with the directive or be subject to the penalties prescribed by this article.

(11) No transient merchant, transient peddler, local peddler or solicitor shall conduct business or set up a sales booth or stand with the city except with the expressed written permission of the owner of the property where business is being conducted.

(Code 1981, § 14-158; Ord. No. 2008-8, § 28.08, 3-1-2004)

(a) Every operator of a game room shall apply for and obtain a license from the city council to operate a game room. Application for such a license shall be made upon forms provided by the city clerk.

(Code 1981, § 14-152; Ord. No. 2008-8, § 28.02, 3-1-2004)

An application fee shall be paid to and collected by the city clerk when the application is submitted to cover the cost of administration of this article.
(Code 1981, § 14-153; Ord. No. 2008-8, § 28.03, 3-1-2004)
822:
The following rules shall be observed by all operators of game rooms within the city:
(1) All game rooms shall observe the hours of operation as set by the city council and shall be subject to changes in hours of operation as set by city council. The current hours of operation are Eastern Standard Time and as follows:
a. Opening time: 7:30 a.m. (7:00 p.m. on Sunday);
b. Closing time: 12:00 a.m. Monday through Saturday.
(2) No play on any game shall be allowed during the times when game rooms are required by this section to remain closed.
(3) All buildings shall conform to the state and city building code, and the operator shall acquire a certificate of compliance before operation shall begin.
(4) No loud offensive noises shall be allowed to emanate beyond the licensed premises.
(5) There must be an adult 18 years of age or older managing the business during hours of operation.
(6) No alcoholic beverages including beer and wine shall be consumed on the premises of a game room or billiards room.
(7) No person under the age of 18 years is permitted on premises of a game room or billiards room before 4:00 p.m. on any day the public or private school's are in session, unless such person is accompanied by his or her parent or legal guardian.

a. Disorderly persons or minors;
b. Intoxicated people or minors to loiter on the premises;
c. Loitering signs must be posted outside premises and security lights must be on at dusk to closing time.
(9) No licensee shall allow the licensed premises to become overcrowded so as to constitute a hazard to the health or safety of persons therein or to be in violation of any of the city's or state's fire, health or sanitation codes.
(10) No game room or billiard room shall be operated so as to constitute a public nuisance.
(Code 1981, § 14-156; Ord. No. 2008-8, § 28.06, 3-1-2004)
823:
(a) After giving the operator or owner of a game room adequate notice and an opportunity to be heard, as provided in this section, the city council may revoke the license of any game room or billiard room operator who:

(2) Is convicted of unlawfully selling alcoholic beverages or narcotic drugs; or
(3) Is convicted of a felony crime.

It shall be unlawful for any person to cast, throw or fling any stone, brickbat or any other such thing of whatever nature on the streets, lanes or alleys, or in any other public place in the city, or out of any premises in the city.

(Code 1981, § 15-7; Ord. No. 1985-7, § 1, 12-16-1985)
834:
(a) A person commits the offense of loitering or prowling when he/she is in a place at a time or in a manner not usual for law-abiding individuals under circumstances that warrant a justifiable and reasonable alarm or immediate concern for the safety of persons or property in the vicinity.
(b) Among the circumstances which may be considered in determining whether alarm is warranted is the fact that the person takes flight upon the appearance of a law enforcement officer, refuses to identify himself/herself, or manifestly endeavors to conceal himself/herself or any object. Unless flight by the person or other circumstances make it impracticable, a law enforcement officer shall, prior to any arrest for an offense under this section, afford the person an opportunity to dispel any alarm or immediate concern which would otherwise be warranted by requesting the person to identify himself/herself and explain his/her presence and conduct. No person shall be convicted of an offense under this section if the law enforcement officer failed to comply with the procedure set forth in this subsection or if it appears at trial that the explanation given by the person was true and would have dispelled the alarm or immediate concern.
(c) A person committing the offense of loitering or prowling shall be subject to imprisonment in the city jail for a period not exceeding six months or a fine not exceeding $1,000.00 or both such fine and imprisonment.

(1) To declare hours of curfew for all persons, and during said hours of curfew, all persons shall be at their homes and shall not be on the streets, alleys or other public areas of the city. (Code 1969, § 11-28; Code 1981, § 15-28)

(a) As used in this section, the term "residential real estate-related transaction" means any of the following:
(1) The making or purchasing of loans or providing other financial assistance:
a. For purchasing, constructing, improving, repairing or maintaining a dwelling;
b. Secured by residential real estate; or
(2) The selling, brokerage, or appraising of residential real property.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person or other entity whose business includes engaging in residential real estate-related transactions to discriminate against any person in making available such a transaction or in the terms or conditions of such a transaction because of race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status or national origin.
(c) Nothing in this article shall be construed to prohibit a person engaged in the business of furnishing appraisals of real property from taking into consideration factors other than race, color, religion, national origin, sex, disability or familial status.

(a) Nothing in this article shall prohibit a religious organization, association, or society, or any nonprofit institution or organization operated, supervised, or controlled by or in conjunction with a religious organization, association or society, from limiting the sale, rental or occupancy of dwellings which it owns or operates for other than a commercial purpose to persons of the same religion or from giving preferences to such persons unless membership in such religion is restricted on account of race, color, sex, disability, familial status or national origin. Nothing in this article shall prohibit a private club not in fact open to the public, which as an incident to its primary purposes provides lodgings which it owns or operates for other than commercial purpose, from limiting the rental or occupancy of such lodgings to its members or from giving preference to its members.
(b) Housing for older persons.
(1) As used in this subsection, the term "housing for older persons" means housing:
a. Provided under any state or federal program that the director determines is specifically designed and operated to assist elderly persons as defined in the state or federal program;
b. Intended for, and solely occupied by persons 62 years of age or older; or
c. Intended and operated for occupancy by at least one person 55 years of age or older per unit. In determining whether housing qualifies as housing for older persons under this subsection (b), the director shall develop regulations which require at least the following factors:
1. The existence of significant facilities and services specifically designed to meet the physical or social needs of older persons, or, if the provision of such facilities and services is not practicable, that such housing is necessary to provide important housing opportunities for older persons;
2. That at least 80 percent of the units are occupied by at least one person 55 years of age or older per unit; and
3. The publication of and adherence to policies and procedures which demonstrate an intent by the owner or manager to provide housing for persons 55 years of age or older.
(2) Nothing in this article limits the applicability of any reasonable local, state or federal restrictions regarding the maximum number of occupants permitted to occupy a dwelling. The provisions in this article regarding familial status shall not apply with respect to housing for older persons.
(3) Housing shall not fail to meet the requirements for housing for older persons by reason of:
a. Persons residing in such housing as of March 12, 1989, who do not meet the age requirements of subsection (b)(1)b or c of this section; provided, however, that new occupants of such housing meet the age requirements of subsection (b)(1)b or c of this section; or
b. Unoccupied units; provided, however, that such units are reserved for occupancy by persons who meet the age requirements of subsection (b)(1)b or c of this section.
(4) Nothing in this article prohibits conduct against a person because such person has been convicted by any court of competent jurisdiction of the illegal manufacture or distribution of a controlled substance.

860:

(Code 1981, § 16-15; Ord. No. 1992-3, 11-16-1992)

(Code 1981, § 16-2; Ord. No. 1992-3, 11-16-1992)

In the interpretation of this and all succeeding park and recreation area ordinances, the provisions shall be construed as follows:
(1) Any term in the singular shall include the plural.
(2) Any term in the masculine shall include the feminine and neuter.
(3) Any requirement or prohibitions of any act, shall respectively extend to and include the causing and procuring, directly or indirectly, of such act.
(4) No provision hereof shall make unlawful any act necessarily performed by any officer or employee of the commission or city in line of duty or work as such, or by any person, his/her agent or employees, in the proper and necessary execution of the terms of any agreement with the commission or city.
(5) Any act otherwise prohibited by law or local ordinance shall be lawful if performed, under, by virtue of, and strictly within the provisions of a permit so to do, and to the extent authorized thereby hereby.
(Code 1981, § 16-3; Ord. No. 1992-3, 11-16-1992)
863:
It shall be unlawful for any person in a public park or recreation area to:
(1) Mark, deface, disfigure, injure, tamper with or displace or remove any buildings, bridges, tables, benches, fireplaces, railings, pavings or paving materials, water lines or other public utilities or parts or appurtenances thereof, signs, notices or placards, whether temporary or permanent, monuments, stakes, posts, or other boundary markers, or other structures or equipment, facilities or park property or appurtenances whatsoever, either real or personal.
(2) Dig or remove any soil, rock, sand, stone, trees, shrubs or plants or other wood or materials, or make any excavation by tool, equipment, blasting or other means or agency.
(3) Construct or erect any building or structure of whatever kind, whether permanent or temporary, or run or string any public service utility into, upon or across such lands, except on special written permit issued hereunder.
(4) Damage, cut, carve, mark, transplant or remove any plant, or injure the bark, or pick flowers or seed of any tree or plant, dig in or otherwise disturb grass areas, or in any other way injure the natural beauty or usefulness of any area.
(5) Throw, discharge, or otherwise place or cause to be placed in the waters of any fountains, pond, lake, stream or other body of water in or adjacent to any park or any tributary stream, storm sewer, or drain flowing into such water, any substance, matter or thing, liquid or solid, which will or may result in the pollution of said waters.

864:
It shall be unlawful for any person in a public park or recreation area to:
(1) Drive any vehicle on any area except the paved park roads of parking areas, or such areas as may on occasion be specifically designated as temporary areas.
(2) Park a vehicle anywhere except on a designated parking area.
(3) Leave a vehicle standing or parked in established parking areas or elsewhere in the park and recreation areas during hours when the park and recreation area is closed. During a snowstorm and for three days thereafter, established parking areas in parks and recreation areas may be utilized for parking, but not by trailers of any kind.
(4) Leave a bicycle in a place other than a bicycle rack when such is provided and there is space available.
(5) Ride a bicycle without reasonable regard for the safety of others.
(6) Leave a bicycle lying on the ground or paving or set against trees, or in any place or position where other persons may trip over or be injured by them.
(7) Wash any vehicle.
(8) Drive or operate within the parks, any bus or vehicle adapted for more than 12 passengers; any hearse, truck or tractor, or vehicle used for advertising provided that taxis, buses, and trucks may be used to carry visitors to the parks and recreation areas.
(9) Use the parks, park drives, parking places or parkways for the purpose of demonstrating any vehicles, or for the purpose of instructing another to drive or operate any vehicle, nor shall any person use any park area, including parking places, for the repairing or cleaning of any vehicle, except in an emergency.

(Code 1981, § 16-5; Ord. No. 1992-3, 11-16-1992)
865:

(1) Any pistol or revolver or objects upon which loaded or blank cartridges may be used. Official starters, at authorized track and field events, are exempted from this restriction.
(2) Any burglar tools.
(3) Any rifle, shotgun, BB gun, air gun, spring gun, slingshot, bow or other weapon in which the propelling force is gunpowder, a spring or air.
(Code 1981, § 16-6; Ord. No. 1992-3, 11-16-1992)

901:
As used in this chapter, the following terms shall have the respective meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Abandoned means an article of machinery, appliance, vehicle, equipment and other material, shall be deemed to have been abandoned or discarded when it has remained upon a property in an inoperable condition for more than ten days, or when it has become inoperable and the owner does not intend to repair it and place it back into operation.
Abandoned vehicle means a vehicle that is in a state of disrepair and incapable of being moved under its own power. It shall be prima facie evidence that a vehicle has been abandoned if the owner or person in possession of such vehicle cannot furnish satisfactory evidence that the motor vehicle license fee required by O.C.G.A. § 48-10-2 has been paid and that the Georgia Motor Vehicle Accident Reparations Act (O.C.G.A. § 33-34-1) has been complied with as respect to such motor vehicle.
Appliance means any type of machine or device used in and about the home or premises, and includes, but shall not be limited to, refrigerators, iceboxes, freezers, stoves, washing machines, clothes dryers, television sets, radio sets, lawn mowers and other devices of like nature.
Automobile graveyard means any establishment which is maintained or used for storing, buying or selling wrecked, scrapped, ruined, dismantled, abandoned or discarded motor vehicles or for motor vehicle repairs.
C & D waste means waste materials generated by construction, remodeling, repair or demolition of residential, commercial or other premises.
Commercial solid waste.
(1) The term "commercial solid waste" means all garbage, trash, refuse, rubbish and other acceptable waste generated by a commercial premises and C & D waste.
(2) The term "commercial solid waste" does not include hazardous waste.
Dealers in junk or metals means any person, partnership firm or corporation who owns, leases, operates or otherwise maintains facilities for processing junk or metals or who buys, sells or in any way deals in any used or discarded metal material or articles.
Dismantler means any person, partnership, firm, or corporation engaged in the business of acquiring wrecked, abandoned or repairable motor vehicles and selling either the usable parts, the motor vehicle as a unit or the hulk of the motor vehicle after the usable parts have been removed. For the purposes of this chapter, a person, partnership, firm or corporation shall be presumed to be engaged in the business of auto dismantling if he/she or it possesses three or more inoperative motor vehicles for more than ten days.
Garbage.
(1) The term "garbage" means organic waste matter, both animal and vegetable, including but not limited to waste matter, from houses, kitchens, restaurants, hotels, hospitals and other such places, and it comprises chiefly waste food.
(2) The term "garbage" does not include moisture that may be drained in the sewer or human body wastes.
Junk means any:
(1) Old or scrap copper, brass, rope, rags, battery, paper, trash, rubber, radiator, debris or waste;
(2) Junked, dismantled or wrecked automobiles, or parts thereof;
(3) Iron, steel, and any other scrap ferrous or nonferrous material; or
(4) Abandoned or discarded machinery, appliance, vehicle, equipment or material of any description or kind whatsoever.
Major component part means one of the following subassemblies of a motor vehicle:
(1) Front clip assembly (fenders, grille and hood);
(2) Rear clip assembly (quarter panels and floor panel assembly);
(3) Engine and transmission;
(4) Top assembly, with the exception of soft tops;
(5) Frame or frame sections; or
(6) Complete side (fenders, door and quarter panel).
Motor vehicle means any vehicle which is self-propelled except trackless trolleys (which are classified as streetcars), motorcycles, motor-driven cycles, or go-carts.
Nuisance means anything that causes hurt, inconvenience or damage to another, and the fact that the act done may otherwise be lawful shall not keep it from being a nuisance. The inconvenience complained of shall not be fanciful, or such as would affect only one of fastidious taste, but shall be such as would affect an ordinary, reasonable man.
Part means any used motor vehicle part that has been installed as standard or optional equipment on a motor vehicle, has been removed from the motor vehicle on which it was originally attached or affixed, and is the subject of sale or resale as a part and not as scrap.
Rebuilder means any person, partnership, firm, or corporation engaged in the business of buying more than three used, salvage, or wrecked motor vehicles per year for the purpose of restoring or rebuilding them with used or new motor vehicle parts, or both, to be sold as motor vehicles.
Salvage dealer means any person, firm or corporation who purchases a salvage vehicle or parts of a salvage vehicle for the purposes of resale as parts only or as salvage.
Salvage vehicle means any vehicle which either:
(1) Has been damaged, crushed, or otherwise reduced to such a state that its restoration would require the replacement of two or more major component parts;
(2) Has been acquired by an insurance company as a result of the vehicle's being damaged to the extent that its restoration to an operable condition would require the replacement of two or more major component parts or for which the insurance company has paid a total loss claim, excluding recovered total theft vehicles which do not require the replacement of two or more major component parts for restoration; or
(3) Is an imported vehicle which has been damaged in shipment and disclaimed by the manufacturer as a result of the damage, has never been the subject of a retail sale to a consumer, and has never been issued a certificate of title.
Scrap processor means any person, firm or corporation engaged in the business of buying or otherwise acquiring iron and metals including, but not limited to, old automobiles, aluminum, glass and parts thereof for the purpose of processing into raw materials for remelting or recycling.
Scrap vehicle means any vehicle which has been wrecked, destroyed, or damaged to the extent that it cannot be economically repaired, rebuilt or made operable or road worthy.
Solid waste means trash and or garbage as defined in this section.
Trash means rubbish such as feathers, paper, cans, bottles, boxes, wood, glass, shrubs, yard clippings, tree trimmings and all similar matter.
Unsafe building means any building or structure that has any of the following conditions, such that the life, health, property or safety of the general public or its occupant are endangered:
(1) Whenever any means of egress or portion thereof is not of adequate size or is not arranged to provide a safe path of travel in case of fire or panic.
(2) Whenever any means of egress of portion thereof, such as but not limited to, fire doors, closing devices, fire-resistive ratings, are in disrepair or in a dilapidated or nonworking condition such that the means of egress could be rendered unsafe in case of fire or panic.
(3) Whenever the stress in any material, member or portion thereof, due to all imposed loads including dead load exceeds the working stresses allowed in the International Building Code (IBC) for new buildings.
(4) Whenever a building, structure or portion thereof has been damaged by fire, flood, earthquake, wind or other cause to the extent that the structural integrity of the buildings or structures is less than it was prior to the damage and is less than the minimum requirement established by the International Building Code (IBC) for new buildings.
(5) Whenever any exterior appendages or portion of a building or structure is not securely fastened, attached or anchored such that it is capable of resisting wind, seismic or similar loads as required by the International Building Code (IBC) for new buildings.
(6) Whenever for any reason a building, structure or portion thereof is manifestly unsafe or unsanitary for the purpose for which it is being used.
(7) Whenever any building, structure or portion thereof as a result of decay, deterioration or dilapidation is likely to fully or partially collapse.
(8) Whenever any building, structure or portion thereof has been constructed or maintained in violation of a specific requirement of the standard codes or of a city, county or state law.
(9) Whenever any building, structure or portion thereof is in such a condition as to constitute a public nuisance.
(10) Whenever any building, structure or portion thereof is unsafe, unsanitary or not provided with adequate egress, or which constitutes a fire hazard, or is otherwise dangerous to human life, or, which in relation to existing use, constitutes a hazard to safety or health by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation, obsolescence or abandonment.
Weed means a plant considered undesirable, unattractive or troublesome, especially one growing where it is not wanted.
(Code 1981, § 11-1; Ord. No. 1987-3, 11-16-1987; Ord. of 6-29-2009)

914:
For the purpose of this article, the following terms, phrases, and words shall have the meaning indicated herein, unless the context indicates otherwise:
City landfill means any landfill or sanitary landfill which is owned, leased or operated by the city or any such landfill or sanitary landfill for which the city has been issued a solid waste handling permit pursuant to the Solid Waste Management Act of the state, whether such permit is held solely by the city or jointly with any other governmental body.
Director means the director of the division of environmental protection of the department of natural resources.
Disposal facility means any facility or location where any treatment, utilization, processing, or deposition of solid waste occurs.
Disposal operation means the performance of solid waste disposal which includes administration, personnel, land, equipment, design and other elements necessary or used in the work of solid waste disposal.
Disposal site means the location where the final deposition of solid waste occurs.
Garbage means food waste including waste accumulations of animal or vegetable matter used or intended for use as food, or that attends the preparation, use, cooking, dealing in or storing of meat, fish, fruit or vegetables.
Landfill means a disposal site where solid wastes, other than putrescible wastes or hazardous wastes, are disposed of using landfilling techniques.
Landfilling means a method of disposing of solid wastes except putrescible wastes or hazardous wastes, on land, by placing an earth cover thereon.
Sanitary landfill means a disposal site where solid wastes are disposed of using sanitary landfilling techniques.
Sanitary landfilling means a method of disposing of putrescible wastes and/or hazardous wastes on land by placing an earth cover thereon.
Scavenge means the uncontrolled picking from discarded solid waste materials.
Solid waste handling means the storage, collection, transportation, treatment, utilization, processing or disposal of solid wastes, or any combination thereof.
Solid waste handling permit means written authorization granted to a person by the director to engage in solid waste handling.
Solid Waste Management Act or the Act, wherever referred to in these rules and regulations, means O.C.G.A. § 12-8-20 et seq.
(Code 1981, § 12-30; Ord. No. 1985-3, § 1, 4-1-1985)
915:
